items.name: encode
items.docs:
The Base64 text of `bytes`, padded with `=` to a multiple of 4.

```roc
expect Base64.encode("foobar".to_utf8()) == "Zm9vYmFy"
```

items.name: decode
items.docs:
The bytes of padded Base64 text. Text whose length is not a multiple of 4,
a character outside the alphabet, or padding anywhere but the end is
`Err(InvalidBase64)`.

```roc
expect Base64.decode("Zm9vYg==") == Ok("foob".to_utf8())
```

items.name: Errors
items.docs: The tags the client adds to the platform's row `e`.
items.head: Errors(e)

items.name: Error
items.docs: Every error of a client call: `Closed`, `Closing` and `Client.Errors(e)`.
items.head: Error(e)

items.name: Transport
items.docs:
What `Client.open!` needs: a byte stream and randomness over one link
value `b`, whose errors are the platform's row with the client's tags.
items.head: Transport(b, e)

items.name: Ops
items.signature: Ws.Core(Client.Conn(b, e), Client.Errors(e), Ws.Ping(Client.Conn(b, e), Client.Errors(e), Ws.Pong(Client.Conn(b, e), Client.Errors(e), Ws.Frames(Client.Conn(b, e), Client.Errors(e), Ws.Poll(Client.Conn(b, e), Client.Errors(e), {})))))
items.docs:
The operations of a client connection as a record, for code generic
over features: the core, ping, pong, frames and poll.
items.head: Ops(b, e)

items.name: Conn
items.docs: An open client connection over the link value `b`, from `Client.open!`.
items.head: Conn(b, e)

items.name: link
items.docs:
The link value as the last call left it, for an adapter that needs
its stream back (to close it, for example).

items.name: map_link
items.docs:
The same connection with its link value changed by `change`, for an
adapter that adjusts its stream between calls (a read timeout for
one call, for example). The protocol state is untouched, so bytes
already read and a half-received message are kept.

items.name: send!
items.signature: Client.Conn(b, e), Ws.Message => Try(Client.Conn(b, e), Client.Error(e))
items.docs: Send one message, in one frame.

items.name: receive!
items.signature: Client.Conn(b, e) => Try((Client.Conn(b, e), Ws.Message), Client.Error(e))
items.docs:
The next message. A platform read deadline passing is not reported:
`receive!` keeps waiting (see `poll!`). After `close!`, it delivers
the messages on their way and ends with `Closed({ by: Us, .. })`.

items.name: poll!
items.signature: Client.Conn(b, e) => Try((Client.Conn(b, e), [Message(Ws.Message), TimedOut]), Client.Error(e))
items.docs:
The next message, or `TimedOut` when the platform's read deadline
passed with no message. Nothing is lost.

items.name: close!
items.signature: Client.Conn(b, e), U16, Str => Try(Client.Conn(b, e), Client.Error(e))
items.docs:
Start the closing handshake: send Close and return. A code that may
not be sent or a reason over 123 bytes is `InvalidClose`.

items.name: ping!
items.signature: Client.Conn(b, e), List(U8) => Try(Client.Conn(b, e), Client.Error(e))
items.docs: Send a Ping, payload at most 125 bytes.

items.name: pong!
items.signature: Client.Conn(b, e), List(U8) => Try(Client.Conn(b, e), Client.Error(e))
items.docs: Send an unsolicited Pong, payload at most 125 bytes.

items.name: send_frame!
items.signature: Client.Conn(b, e), Frame => Try(Client.Conn(b, e), Client.Error(e))
items.docs: Send any frame, masked. A frame that breaks RFC 6455 is `BadFrame`.

items.name: receive_frame!
items.signature: Client.Conn(b, e) => Try((Client.Conn(b, e), Frame), Client.Error(e))
items.docs:
The next frame as it arrives: no assembly, no reply. Do not mix it
with `receive!` inside a fragmented message.

items.name: default_max_message
items.docs: The largest message accepted when the request does not say: 16 MiB.

items.name: ops
items.docs: The operations as a record, for code generic over features.

items.name: open!
items.signature: Client.Transport(b, e), b, Ws.ConnectRequest => Try(Ws.Opened(Client.Conn(b, e)), Client.Error(e))
items.docs:
Do the opening handshake over a connected link and return the
connection. `request.url` gives the `Host` header and the resource; the
adapter has already connected to its host and port (and done TLS for
`wss://`). A refused upgrade, the stream ending during it, or no answer
before the platform's read deadline is `Refused`.

items.name: normal
items.docs: 1000: the purpose of the connection is fulfilled.

items.name: going_away
items.docs: 1001: the endpoint goes away (server shutdown, page left).

items.name: protocol_error
items.docs: 1002: the peer broke the protocol.

items.name: unsupported_data
items.docs: 1003: a kind of data the endpoint cannot accept.

items.name: no_status
items.docs: 1005: the Close frame had no code. Reported, never sent.

items.name: abnormal
items.docs: 1006: the connection dropped with no Close frame. Reported, never sent.

items.name: invalid_payload
items.docs: 1007: a text message was not UTF-8.

items.name: policy_violation
items.docs: 1008: the message breaks the endpoint's policy.

items.name: too_big
items.docs: 1009: a message too big to process.

items.name: mandatory_extension
items.docs: 1010: the client expected an extension the server did not negotiate.

items.name: internal_error
items.docs: 1011: the server hit an unexpected condition.

items.name: is_sendable
items.docs:
Whether an endpoint may put `code` in a Close frame: 1000-1003,
1007-1014 (1012-1014 registered with IANA after RFC 6455), and
3000-4999 (libraries and applications). 1004, 1005, 1006 and 1015 are
reserved and never sent.

items.name: payload
items.docs:
The payload of a Close frame: the code, big-endian, then the reason as
UTF-8, at most 123 bytes so the frame stays within 125.

items.name: parse
items.signature: List(U8) -> Try({ code : U16, reason : Str, has_code : Bool }, [Invalid({ code : U16, why : Str })])
items.docs:
The code and reason of a received Close payload. An empty payload is
code 1005 and no reason. A 1-byte payload, a code that may not be sent,
or a reason that is not UTF-8 is `Err`, with the code to fail the
connection with (1002 or 1007).

items.name: Frame
items.signature: { fin : Bool, opcode : Frame.Opcode, payload : List(U8) }
items.docs:
One WebSocket frame (RFC 6455 section 5.2), with its payload unmasked.

Extensions are not supported, so the RSV bits are always 0: a frame with
one set is invalid.
items.head: Frame

items.name: Opcode
items.docs:
What a frame carries. `Continuation` continues a fragmented message;
`Close`, `Ping` and `Pong` are control frames.
items.head: Opcode

items.name: Masking
items.docs:
Whether frames are masked. A client masks every frame it sends with
4 unpredictable bytes; a server never masks (RFC 6455 section 5.3).
items.head: Masking

items.name: Expect
items.docs:
Which masking the receiver requires: a server requires masked frames, a
client unmasked ones.
items.head: Expect

items.name: Header
items.signature:
{
		fin : Bool,
		opcode : Frame.Opcode,
		mask : Frame.Masking,
		length : U64,
		## Bytes of the header: 2 to 14.
		size : U64,
	}
items.docs: The fixed part of a frame, read before its payload.
items.head: Header

items.name: text
items.docs: A whole text message in one frame.

items.name: binary
items.docs: A whole binary message in one frame.

items.name: ping
items.docs: A ping. The payload is at most 125 bytes.

items.name: pong
items.docs: A pong. The payload is at most 125 bytes.

items.name: is_control
items.docs: Whether the opcode is a control opcode.

items.name: code
items.docs: The 4-bit code of an opcode.

items.name: mask
items.docs:
XOR `bytes` with the 4-byte `key`, repeated (RFC 6455 section 5.3).
Masking twice with one key gives the original bytes.

items.name: encode
items.docs:
The bytes of a frame on the wire. A control frame payload must be at most
125 bytes and a control frame must be final; a mask must be 4 bytes.

items.name: header
items.docs:
The header at the start of `bytes`. `Incomplete(n)` means the header
needs `n` bytes in all. `Invalid` names the RFC rule the frame breaks.

items.name: decode
items.signature: List(U8), Frame.Expect -> Try({ frame : Frame, rest : List(U8) }, [Incomplete(U64), Invalid(Str)])
items.docs:
The first frame of `bytes`, unmasked, and the bytes after it.
`Incomplete(n)` means the frame needs `n` bytes in all, so a reader
that reads `n - bytes.len()` more bytes never reads past the frame.

items.name: fragments
items.docs:
The frames of one message, each payload at most `size` bytes (at least 1).
The first frame has the message's opcode, the others are
`Continuation`, and only the last is final.

items.name: Url
items.signature: { secure : Bool, host : Str, port : U16, resource : Str }
items.docs:
A parsed `ws://` or `wss://` URL. `resource` is the path and query,
`/` when the URL has none.
items.head: Url

items.name: Header
items.docs: A header, its name as received.
items.head: Header

items.name: ClientRequest
items.docs: What a client asks for. `key` is 16 random bytes.
items.head: ClientRequest

items.name: Agreed
items.signature: { protocol : Str, extensions : List(Str), headers : List(Handshake.Header) }
items.docs:
What the server agreed to. `protocol` is `""` when the server chose no
subprotocol.
items.head: Agreed

items.name: Upgrade
items.signature: { resource : Str, host : Str, key : Str, protocols : List(Str), headers : List(Handshake.Header) }
items.docs:
A request head a server received, validated as a WebSocket upgrade.
`key` is the client's `Sec-WebSocket-Key` text.
items.head: Upgrade

items.name: guid
items.docs: The GUID that RFC 6455 section 1.3 appends to the key.

items.name: accept_key
items.docs:
`Sec-WebSocket-Accept` for a `Sec-WebSocket-Key`: Base64 of the SHA-1 of
the key and the GUID.

```roc
expect Handshake.accept_key("dGhlIHNhbXBsZSBub25jZQ==") == "s3pPLMBiTxaQ9kYGzzhZRbK+xOo="
```

items.name: parse_url
items.docs:
Parse `ws://host[:port][/path][?query]` or `wss://...`. The default port is
80 for `ws` and 443 for `wss`. A fragment (`#...`) is not allowed
(RFC 6455 section 3). An IPv6 host is written in brackets.

items.name: client_request
items.docs:
The request head a client sends: an HTTP/1.1 `GET` with the upgrade
headers, then `headers`. The `Host` header has the port when it is not
the default one.

items.name: check_response
items.docs:
Check the server's response head against the request (RFC 6455
section 4.1, the client's checks): status 101, `Upgrade: websocket`,
`Connection: Upgrade`, the right `Sec-WebSocket-Accept`, no extension,
and a subprotocol only if it is one the client offered.

items.name: parse_upgrade
items.signature: Str -> Try(Handshake.Upgrade, [Rejected({ status : U16, why : Str })])
items.docs:
Validate a request head as a WebSocket upgrade (RFC 6455 section
4.2.1, the server's checks). `Err(Rejected({ status, why }))` gives
the status to answer with (400, 405, or 426 for a wrong version) and
`Handshake.rejection` writes that answer.

items.name: accept_response
items.docs:
The server's 101 response to a valid upgrade, with the subprotocol it
chose (`""` for none; it must be one the client offered) and extra
headers.

items.name: choose_protocol
items.docs:
The first protocol of `supported`, the server's order of preference,
that the client offered, or `""`.

items.name: rejection
items.docs:
A refusal of an upgrade: the status, `Sec-WebSocket-Version: 13` for a
426, and `why` as the body.

items.name: refusal
items.docs:
A response refusing an upgrade: the status line, `Sec-WebSocket-Version: 13`
for a 426 (RFC 6455 section 4.4), the extra `headers`, and `body` as
plain text. It ends with `Connection: close`.

items.name: head_end
items.docs:
The index just after the first `\r\n\r\n` that starts at or after
`from`: the end of an HTTP head and the start of the bytes after it.
A reader that appends bytes searches from 3 before the new ones.

items.name: head_wanted
items.docs:
How many more bytes a reader can read without passing the end of an
HTTP head (`\r\n\r\n`), given the bytes read so far: 0 when `bytes`
already ends the head. A reader that reads at most this many bytes
never takes bytes of the first frame.

items.name: Protocol
items.signature:
{
	role : [Client, Server],
	max_message : U64,
	phase : [Open, Closing({ code : U16, reason : Str }), Done(Ws.Closure)],
	pending : List(U8),
	partial : [Idle, Partial({ kind : [Text, Binary], bytes : List(U8) })],
}
items.docs:
The receiving side of RFC 6455 as a state machine with no I/O: feed it
bytes, get events. It checks every frame, assembles fragments into
messages, answers Ping and Close, fails the connection on a protocol error,
and tracks the closing handshake.

A driver keeps the `Protocol` between reads: it reads any number of
bytes, calls `receive`, writes each `Write` frame (masked with
`Protocol.masking` for a client), and acts on the other events. Bytes after
the last whole frame stay in the state until more arrive.
items.head: Protocol

items.name: Event
items.docs:
What one call of `receive` produced, in order.
- `Message`: a whole message.
- `Write`: a frame to send now (a Pong, the Close echo, or the Close that
  fails the connection).
- `Ping`, `Pong`: a control frame arrived (a Ping is answered by a
  `Write` already).
- `Closed`: the connection has ended; nothing more follows.
items.head: Event

items.name: new
items.docs:
A protocol in the open state, for an endpoint of `role`, accepting
messages of at most `max_message` bytes.

items.name: is_open
items.docs: Whether messages may still be sent: no Close was sent or received.

items.name: is_done
items.docs: Whether the connection has ended.

items.name: closure
items.docs: How the connection ended, once it has.

items.name: closing
items.signature: Protocol -> Try({ code : U16, reason : Str }, [NotClosing])
items.docs: The Close this endpoint sent and is waiting to see answered.

items.name: is_idle
items.docs: Whether no frame or message is half received.

items.name: wanted
items.docs:
How many bytes the current frame still needs at least. Reading at most
this many never reads past the frame. 0 once the connection has ended.

items.name: masking
items.docs:
The masking for a frame this endpoint sends: a client masks with `key`,
4 random bytes; a server does not mask.

items.name: expects
items.docs:
The masking a received frame must have: a server expects masked frames,
a client unmasked ones.

items.name: receive
items.docs: Feed received bytes, any number of them.

items.name: close
items.signature: Protocol, U16, Str -> Try((Protocol, Frame), [NotOpen, InvalidCode(U16), ReasonTooLong(U64)])
items.docs:
Start the closing handshake: the Close frame to send. Afterwards
`receive` still delivers messages until the peer's Close arrives, which
ends the connection with `Closed({ by: Us, .. })`.

items.name: fail
items.docs:
Fail the connection (RFC 6455 section 7.1.7): the Close with `code` to
send (unless a Close was sent already) and the `Closed` event.

items.name: pending_bytes
items.docs: The received bytes not yet consumed: the start of the next frame.

items.name: max_message
items.docs: The largest message accepted, in bytes.

items.name: push
items.docs:
Add received bytes without processing them, for a driver that reads
raw frames with `take_frame`.

items.name: take_frame
items.docs:
The next whole frame of the received bytes as it is: no assembly, no
reply, no state change but removing its bytes.

items.name: ended
items.docs:
The transport ended with no Close frame (the peer closed the TCP
connection, or a read failed for good): the connection is done, with
code 1006.

items.name: Errors
items.docs:
The tags the server adds to the platform's row `e`: `NotUpgrade(why)`
for a request that is not a valid upgrade (answered with a refusal
already), `InvalidStatus(status)` for a refusal status that is not a
final HTTP status (200-599, so never 101), and the frame tags of
`Client.Errors`.
items.head: Errors(e)

items.name: Error
items.docs: Every error of a server call: `Closed`, `Closing` and `Server.Errors(e)`.
items.head: Error(e)

items.name: Transport
items.docs:
What the server needs: a byte stream over a link value `b`, whose
errors are the platform's row with the server's tags. No randomness.
items.head: Transport(b, e)

items.name: Ops
items.signature: Ws.Core(Server.Conn(b, e), Server.Errors(e), Ws.Ping(Server.Conn(b, e), Server.Errors(e), Ws.Pong(Server.Conn(b, e), Server.Errors(e), Ws.Frames(Server.Conn(b, e), Server.Errors(e), Ws.Poll(Server.Conn(b, e), Server.Errors(e), {})))))
items.docs:
The operations of a server connection as a record, for code generic
over features: the core, ping, pong, frames and poll.
items.head: Ops(b, e)

items.name: Conn
items.docs:
An open server connection over the link value `b`, from
`Server.accept!` or `request.accept!`.
items.head: Conn(b, e)

items.name: link
items.docs:
The link value as the last call left it, for an adapter that needs
its stream back (to close it, for example).

items.name: map_link
items.docs:
The same connection with its link value changed by `change` (a
read timeout for one call, for example). The protocol state is
untouched.

items.name: send!
items.signature: Server.Conn(b, e), Ws.Message => Try(Server.Conn(b, e), Server.Error(e))
items.docs: Send one message, in one unmasked frame.

items.name: receive!
items.signature: Server.Conn(b, e) => Try((Server.Conn(b, e), Ws.Message), Server.Error(e))
items.docs:
The next message. A platform read deadline passing is not reported:
`receive!` keeps waiting (see `poll!`). After `close!`, it delivers
the messages on their way and ends with `Closed({ by: Us, .. })`.

items.name: poll!
items.signature: Server.Conn(b, e) => Try((Server.Conn(b, e), [Message(Ws.Message), TimedOut]), Server.Error(e))
items.docs:
The next message, or `TimedOut` when the platform's read deadline
passed with no message. Nothing is lost.

items.name: close!
items.signature: Server.Conn(b, e), U16, Str => Try(Server.Conn(b, e), Server.Error(e))
items.docs:
Start the closing handshake: send Close and return. A code that may
not be sent or a reason over 123 bytes is `InvalidClose`. Once
`receive!` gives `Closed`, the adapter closes the stream (RFC 6455
section 7.1.1: the server closes the TCP connection first).

items.name: ping!
items.signature: Server.Conn(b, e), List(U8) => Try(Server.Conn(b, e), Server.Error(e))
items.docs: Send a Ping, payload at most 125 bytes.

items.name: pong!
items.signature: Server.Conn(b, e), List(U8) => Try(Server.Conn(b, e), Server.Error(e))
items.docs: Send an unsolicited Pong, payload at most 125 bytes.

items.name: send_frame!
items.signature: Server.Conn(b, e), Frame => Try(Server.Conn(b, e), Server.Error(e))
items.docs: Send any frame, unmasked. A frame that breaks RFC 6455 is `BadFrame`.

items.name: receive_frame!
items.signature: Server.Conn(b, e) => Try((Server.Conn(b, e), Frame), Server.Error(e))
items.docs:
The next frame as it arrives, unmasked: no assembly, no reply. Do
not mix it with `receive!` inside a fragmented message.

items.name: Request
items.signature: { transport : Server.Transport(b, e), link : b, upgrade : Handshake.Upgrade, rest : List(U8) }
items.docs:
An upgrade request read from the link and validated, not answered
yet, from `Server.read_request!`. It keeps the bytes the client sent
after the request head, the start of its first frames.
items.head: Request(b, e)

items.name: map_link
items.docs:
The same request with its link value changed by `change`, for an
adapter that reads the request with one deadline and runs the
connection with another (a short handshake timeout, for example).

items.name: upgrade
items.docs:
The request: its resource, `Host`, the subprotocols the client
offered in order, and every header (names lowercased).

items.name: accept!
items.signature: Server.Request(b, e), Ws.AcceptOptions => Try(Ws.Opened(Server.Conn(b, e)), Server.Error(e))
items.docs:
Accept the upgrade: write the 101 response with the first
subprotocol of `options.protocols` that the client offered (the
server's order of preference; none when nothing matches), and
return the connection. No
extension is accepted, so `extensions` is `Reported([])`. Bytes the
client sent after its request are then read as frames.

To choose a subprotocol another way, pick one from
`request.upgrade().protocols` and pass `protocols: [chosen]`.

items.name: refuse!
items.docs:
Refuse the upgrade: write a response with `refusal.status`, its
headers and body, and give the link back for the adapter to close.
Any final status is allowed (a 3xx with a `Location` header, a 401
with `WWW-Authenticate`, a 4xx or 5xx). A status outside 200-599
(a 1xx, 101 among them, which ends no exchange, or no HTTP status)
is `InvalidStatus` and writes nothing.

```roc
link = request.refuse!({ status: 403, body: "no access to ${request.upgrade().resource}" })?
```

items.name: default_max_message
items.docs: The largest message accepted when the options do not say: 16 MiB.

items.name: max_request_head
items.docs:
The largest request head accepted, `\r\n\r\n` included: 16 KiB. A
longer one is answered with 431.

items.name: ops
items.docs:
The operations as a record, for code generic over features
(`Ws.drive!`, `Ws.close_and_wait!`, `Ws.messages`).

items.name: read_request!
items.signature: Server.Transport(b, e), b => Try(Server.Request(b, e), Server.Error(e))
items.docs:
Read the upgrade request from a link the adapter has accepted, and
validate it (RFC 6455 section 4.2.1). Each read asks for at most the
bytes still allowed by `max_request_head`, and bytes after the head are
kept in the request.

A request that is not a valid upgrade is answered (400, 405, 426, or
431 for a head over `max_request_head`) and gives `NotUpgrade(why)`;
the stream ending, or the platform's read deadline passing, before the
end of the head gives `NotUpgrade(why)` with nothing written.

items.name: accept!
items.signature: Server.Transport(b, e), b, Ws.AcceptOptions => Try(Ws.Opened(Server.Conn(b, e)), Server.Error(e))
items.docs:
Read the request and accept it with `options`: `read_request!`, then
`request.accept!(options)`.

items.name: Session
items.signature:
{
	bytes : Ws.Bytes(b, Session.Errors(e), {}),
	mask! : b => Try((b, Frame.Masking), Ws.Error(Session.Errors(e))),
	link : b,
	protocol : Protocol,
	inbox : List(Ws.Message),
	held : List(Frame),
}
items.docs:
Frame I/O over a byte link after the opening handshake, for either role.
`Client.Conn` and `Server.Conn` each hold one and forward their methods to
it. Not exposed by the package.

The roles differ only in `mask!` (a client masks each frame it sends with 4
random bytes, a server does not mask) and in the `Protocol`'s role, which
sets the masking a received frame must have.

The peer's Close is answered once the messages read with it are delivered:
when one read brings messages and the Close, the echo is held (`held`)
until a call finds the inbox empty, so replies to those messages are sent
before it (RFC 6455 section 5.5.1 lets an endpoint delay its echo).
items.head: Session(b, e)

items.name: Errors
items.docs: The tags frame I/O adds to the row `e` of its role.
items.head: Errors(e)

items.name: Error
items.docs: Every error of a session call.
items.head: Error(e)

items.name: start!
items.signature: Ws.Bytes(b, Session.Errors(e), {}), (b => Try((b, Frame.Masking), Session.Error(e))), b, Protocol, List(U8) => Try(Session(b, e), Session.Error(e))
items.docs:
A session over a link the handshake has just finished on, fed the
bytes read after the handshake head. The frames those bytes provoke (a
Pong, a Close) are written.

items.name: link
items.docs: The link value as the last call left it.

items.name: map_link
items.docs: The same session with its link value changed by `change`.

items.name: send!
items.signature: Session(b, e), Ws.Message => Try(Session(b, e), Session.Error(e))

items.name: receive!
items.signature: Session(b, e) => Try((Session(b, e), Ws.Message), Session.Error(e))

items.name: poll!
items.signature: Session(b, e) => Try((Session(b, e), [Message(Ws.Message), TimedOut]), Session.Error(e))

items.name: close!
items.signature: Session(b, e), U16, Str => Try(Session(b, e), Session.Error(e))

items.name: ping!
items.signature: Session(b, e), List(U8) => Try(Session(b, e), Session.Error(e))

items.name: pong!
items.signature: Session(b, e), List(U8) => Try(Session(b, e), Session.Error(e))

items.name: send_frame!
items.signature: Session(b, e), Frame => Try(Session(b, e), Session.Error(e))

items.name: receive_frame!
items.signature: Session(b, e) => Try((Session(b, e), Frame), Session.Error(e))

items.name: default_max_message
items.docs:
The largest message accepted when the request or the options do not
say: 16 MiB.

items.name: hash
items.docs: The 20-byte digest of `bytes`.

items.name: hex
items.docs: The digest as 40 lowercase hex digits.

items.name: Error
items.docs:
Every error of an effectful field: the connection has ended
(`Closed`), this endpoint can no longer send and does not know the
closure yet (`Closing`), or a tag of the adapter's row `e`.
items.head: Error(e)

items.name: Message
items.docs: One whole message.
items.head: Message

items.name: Closure
items.signature: { code : U16, reason : Str, clean : Bool, by : [Peer, Us, Transport] }
items.docs:
How a connection ended (RFC 6455 section 7). `code` is 1005 when the
Close frame had no code and 1006 when the connection dropped with no
Close frame. `clean` is whether both Close frames were exchanged. `by`
is who started the close: the peer, this endpoint (by `close!` or by
failing the connection after a protocol error), or the transport.
items.head: Closure

items.name: ConnectRequest
items.signature: { url : Str, protocols ?: List(Str), headers ?: List((Str, Str)), max_message ?: U64 }
items.docs:
A request to open a client connection. `protocols` are the
subprotocols offered in order (default none), `headers` extra request
headers (default none), `max_message` the largest message accepted, in
bytes. With no `max_message` the adapter's own limit applies (16 MiB
over bytes, `Client.default_max_message`). A bigger message fails the
connection with 1009: `receive!` gives
`Closed({ code: 1009, by: Us, clean: Bool.False, .. })`.
items.head: ConnectRequest

items.name: Opened
items.signature: { conn : c, protocol : Str, extensions : [Reported(List(Str)), NotReported] }
items.docs:
An open connection `conn`, with what the handshake settled: the chosen
subprotocol (`""` for none) and the extensions, `Reported(list)` (an
empty list for none) or `NotReported` where the platform does not tell
(a runtime that negotiates and applies an extension by itself).
items.head: Opened(c)

items.name: AcceptOptions
items.docs:
Options of a server accepting an upgrade: the subprotocols it supports,
in order of preference (default none), and `max_message`, the largest
message accepted, in bytes. The chosen subprotocol is the first of
`protocols` that the client offered, whatever the order of its offer;
none when nothing matches. With no `max_message` the adapter's own
limit applies (16 MiB over bytes, `Server.default_max_message`). A
bigger message fails the connection with 1009: `receive!` gives
`Closed({ code: 1009, by: Us, clean: Bool.False, .. })`.
items.head: AcceptOptions

items.name: Upgrade
items.signature: { resource : Str, host : Str, protocols : List(Str), headers : List((Str, Str)) }
items.docs:
An upgrade request as a server sees it before it accepts or refuses:
the resource (path and query), `Host`, the subprotocols the client
offered in its order, and every header, its name lowercased.
items.head: Upgrade

items.name: Refusal
items.signature: { status : U16, headers ?: List((Str, Str)), body ?: Str }
items.docs:
How a server refuses an upgrade: a final HTTP status, 200 to 599 (RFC
6455 section 4.2.2 allows any status but 101), such as 401 with a
`WWW-Authenticate` header or a 3xx with a `Location`; extra response
headers (default none); a plain-text body (default none). How a refusal is sent is the platform's: a byte
server writes it, a request handler returns it as its response.
items.head: Refusal

items.name: Core
items.signature: { send! : c, Ws.Message => Try(c, Ws.Error(e)), receive! : c => Try((c, Ws.Message), Ws.Error(e)), close! : c, U16, Str => Try(c, Ws.Error(e)), ..r }
items.docs:
What every connection can do on every platform.

- `send!` sends one message.
- `receive!` waits for the next message. `Err(Closed(_))` once the
  connection has ended.
- `close!` starts the closing handshake: it sends Close and returns at
  once. `receive!` then delivers the messages already on their way and
  ends with `Closed({ by: Us, .. })` when the peer answers. Until then,
  `send!` and a second `close!` give `Closing`.
  `Ws.close_and_wait!` does both.
items.head: Core(c, e, r)

items.name: Sender
items.signature: { send! : c, Ws.Message => Try(c, Ws.Error(e)), close! : c, U16, Str => Try(c, Ws.Error(e)), ..r }
items.docs:
The sending half alone, for a push-model server whose messages arrive
as `Handlers` calls rather than by `receive!`.
items.head: Sender(c, e, r)

items.name: Ping
items.docs:
Send a protocol-level Ping (RFC 6455 section 5.5.2), payload at most 125
bytes. The peer's Pong is not reported by `receive!`; read it with
`Frames`.
items.head: Ping(c, e, r)

items.name: Pong
items.docs: Send an unsolicited Pong, a one-way heartbeat (RFC 6455 section 5.5.3).
items.head: Pong(c, e, r)

items.name: Frames
items.signature: { send_frame! : c, Frame => Try(c, Ws.Error(e)), receive_frame! : c => Try((c, Frame), Ws.Error(e)), ..r }
items.docs:
Frame-level access: send any frame (fragments, control frames) and read
the next frame as it arrives, with no assembly and no automatic reply.
A received frame that breaks the protocol fails the connection.
items.head: Frames(c, e, r)

items.name: ReceiveWithin
items.signature: { receive_within! : c, U64 => Try((c, [Message(Ws.Message), TimedOut]), Ws.Error(e)), ..r }
items.docs:
A receive that waits at most `ms` milliseconds. `TimedOut` loses
nothing.
items.head: ReceiveWithin(c, e, r)

items.name: Poll
items.docs:
A receive that waits only as long as the platform's own read deadline
(a fixed time the application does not choose), then gives `TimedOut`,
as `ReceiveWithin` does. `TimedOut` loses nothing.
items.head: Poll(c, e, r)

items.name: Buffered
items.docs: The bytes queued for sending and not yet handed to the network.
items.head: Buffered(c, e, r)

items.name: AutoResponse
items.signature: { set_auto_response! : c, { request : Str, response : Str } => Try(c, Ws.Error(e)), clear_auto_response! : c => Try(c, Ws.Error(e)), ..r }
items.docs:
A fixed text reply that the runtime sends to a fixed text request by
itself, without running application code (an application-level
heartbeat that does not wake the server). `c` is the scope the runtime
sets it for: a connection, or a whole server (every connection it
holds) on a runtime that keeps one reply per server.
items.head: AutoResponse(c, e, r)

items.name: Persist
items.signature: { saved! : c => Try([Saved(List(U8)), Nothing], Ws.Error(e)), save! : c, List(U8) => Try(c, Ws.Error(e)), ..r }
items.docs:
Per-connection state kept by the runtime, which survives the server
leaving memory while the connection stays open (hibernation).
items.head: Persist(c, e, r)

items.name: Topics
items.signature: { subscribe! : c, Str => Try(c, Ws.Error(e)), unsubscribe! : c, Str => Try(c, Ws.Error(e)), publish! : c, Str, Ws.Message => Try(c, Ws.Error(e)), ..r }
items.docs:
Named groups of connections, with one send to every member
(publish/subscribe).
items.head: Topics(c, e, r)

items.name: Connect
items.docs:
Open a client connection `c`. A server that refuses the upgrade is
`Refused(Str)` in `e`.
items.head: Connect(c, e, r)

items.name: Accept
items.signature: { accept! : q, Ws.AcceptOptions => Try({ response : p, opened : Ws.Opened(c) }, Ws.Error(e)), ..r }
items.docs:
Accept an upgrade of an incoming request `q` into a server connection
`c`. `response` is the handshake response `p` that the application
hands back to its runtime, on a platform where the request handler
returns the 101 response (the connection then lives in work that runs
after it); `{}` where `accept!` writes the response itself. A request
that is not a valid upgrade is `NotUpgrade(Str)` in `e`.
items.head: Accept(q, p, c, e, r)

items.name: Handlers
items.docs:
Callbacks of a push-model server, where the runtime delivers events.
`s` is the application's state, threaded from call to call, and `c` the
connection, used with the adapter's `Sender` fields. On a runtime that
does not keep the server in memory between events, the adapter stores
`s` (for example through `Persist`) or the application keeps `s` as `{}`.

`on_close!` gets the connection too, after it has ended: for what the
value holds (an adapter's link to close, a connection id to forget, a
`Persist` attachment to read). Sending on it gives `Closed`. It returns
no connection, since nothing follows it.
items.head: Handlers(s, c, e)

items.name: Bytes
items.signature: { write_bytes! : b, List(U8) => Try(b, Ws.Error(e)), read_up_to! : b, U64 => Try((b, [Data(List(U8)), End, TimedOut]), Ws.Error(e)), ..r }
items.docs:
A byte stream `b`, for a platform where Roc owns the wire (TCP).
`read_up_to!(b, n)` gives `Data` of 1 to `n` bytes, `End` at the end of
the stream, or `TimedOut` when a platform deadline passed with nothing
to read (it consumes nothing).
items.head: Bytes(b, e, r)

items.name: Random
items.signature: { random_bytes! : b, U64 => Try((b, List(U8)), Ws.Error(e)), ..r }
items.docs:
Unpredictable bytes (RFC 6455 section 10.3) for the client's key and
masks: `random_bytes!(b, n)` gives exactly `n` bytes. `b` may carry a
generator's state.
items.head: Random(b, e, r)

items.name: Basic
items.docs: A connection with only the core.
items.head: Basic(c, e)

items.name: Raw
items.signature: Ws.Core(c, e, Ws.Ping(c, e, Ws.Pong(c, e, Ws.Frames(c, e, {}))))
items.docs: A connection over raw bytes: the core, ping, pong and frames.
items.head: Raw(c, e)

items.name: Timed
items.docs: A connection with the core and a receive with a deadline.
items.head: Timed(c, e)

items.name: Push
items.docs: A push-model server connection: sending only, events by callback.
items.head: Push(c, e)

items.name: Transport
items.docs:
What the pure client needs from a platform: a byte stream and
randomness over one link state `b`.
items.head: Transport(b, e)

items.name: messages
items.signature: { receive! : c => Try((c, Ws.Message), Ws.Error(e)), .. }, c -> Stream(Try(Ws.Message, Ws.Error(e)))
items.docs:
The messages of a connection as a stream. The last item is the `Err`
that ended it: `Err(Closed(closure))` once the connection has ended, or
another error of `receive!`.

items.name: close_and_wait!
items.signature: { close! : c, U16, Str => Try(c, Ws.Error(e)), receive! : c => Try((c, Ws.Message), Ws.Error(e)), .. }, c, U16, Str => Try(Ws.Closure, Ws.Error(e))
items.docs:
Close and wait for the end of the closing handshake, dropping the
messages that arrive meanwhile. A connection that is closing already
(`close!` gives `Closing`) is waited for as it is.

items.name: drive!
items.signature: { receive! : c => Try((c, Ws.Message), Ws.Error(e)), .. }, c, s, Ws.Handlers(s, c, e) => (s, Try(Ws.Closure, Ws.Error(e)))
items.docs:
Run push handlers over a pull connection until it closes: `on_open!`,
`on_message!` for each message, then `on_close!` with the connection
as the last call left it and the closure.

The result is the state and how the run ended, both ways: `(s,
Ok(closure))` after `on_close!`, whose state it is, or `(s, Err(err))`
with the state as the last handler that succeeded left it (the initial
state when `on_open!` fails). So an error does not lose the state:

```roc
(count, ended) = Ws.drive!(ops, conn, 0, handlers)
save!(count)
closure = ended?
```

A handler that fails with `Closed` (it sent on a connection that had
ended, such as one whose stream dropped with messages still to deliver)
does not end the run: the messages left are delivered from the
connection as it was before that call, then `on_close!` runs. Any other
handler error, or an error of `receive!` other than `Closed`, ends the
run with that error and no `on_close!`.

items.name: dropped
items.docs: The closure of a connection that dropped with no Close frame.
